title: Help buttons on every form
one: A question-mark button on each panel that says what to do.

screens.title: Check the parts this chapter needs
screens.goal: Before I start, I check that every panel and form has its own ? button.

blocks.p: This chapter uses work from earlier chapters. This screen checks that it is there.

check.what: Does every panel on frmDataEntry have a ? button, with a name that starts btnHelp?
check.how: Open frmDataEntry in the Design tab. Click each ? button and look at its Name.

check.what: Does the login form have a ? button?
check.how: Open frmLogin in the Design tab. Look for the ? button.

check.what: Does the quiz form have a ? button in its score panel?
check.how: Open frmQuiz in the Design tab. Look inside the score panel.

check.what: Does the reaction test form have a ? button?
check.how: Open frmTest in the Design tab. Look inside the score panel.

screens.title: Make the pupil details ? button speak
screens.goal: Clicking the ? in the pupil details panel shows a message that says what to do.

blocks.p: In the Design tab, double-click the ? button in the pupil details panel. Its click code opens in the code tab.

screens.title: Try every help button
screens.goal: I run the program and click every ? button, and a locked one does nothing.

blocks.p: Run your program. Then try each row.

check.how: YOUR login message shows. Click OK to close it.

check.what: Log in. Click the ? in the pupil details panel.
check.how: YOUR message for that panel shows.

check.what: Work through the panels. Click each ? while its panel is on.
check.how: Each panel shows its own message.

check.what: Take the quiz and the test. Click the ? on each form.
check.how: Each form shows its own message.

check.what: Click Calculate in the group panel. When the group appears, the panel goes grey. Click its ? now.
check.how: Nothing must happen, because the whole panel is switched off.
check.fix: If a message shows, look at chapter 10, screen 3-7.
